item.title: A sparse bilinear form with mean oscillations
item.description: arXiv:2611.33783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we establish an oscillatory sparse domination for the bilinear forms associated with Calder\'on-Zygmund operators. We further characterize this oscillatory sparse domination in terms of either the boundedness of $T1$ or local endpoint Orlicz norm estimates. Our method also applies to recover Lerner's Sobolev-type inequality in \cite{L2026}.
item.dc:creator: Jinsong Li

item.title: Random dyadic shift scattering: scale-uniform deformation stability and phase-aligned Hilbert multipliers
item.description:
arXiv:2611.33907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Petermichl's theorem represents the Hilbert transform by averaging a single dyadic shift over dilations and random dyadic lattices. We study how the deformation stability of the lattice-averaged shift, and of a parameter-free feature map $\Phi$ built from it in the spirit of Mallat's wavelet scattering, depends on the number $J+1$ of scales. For the Haar generator as well as compactly supported $C^1$ orthonormal wavelets, the covariance error under a deformation $f\mapsto f(\cdot-	au(\cdot))$ is $O((J+1)
orm{	au'}_\infty
orm f)$ without a $
orm	au_\infty$ term, because lattice averaging absorbs the translation part of $	au$ exactly. The deformation defect splits into a first-order Calder'on commutator, bounded uniformly in $J$ by the $T(1)$ theorem, and a second-order remainder. On a single lattice, affine warps and $C^{1,\delta}$ generators give a lower bound $c\,\sigma_\eps\sqrt{J+1}-C\eps$ for the defect, with an explicit constant $\sigma_\eps\ge0$ computed to be positive for sym4 and db4 at three values of $\eps$. Averaging over lattices turns the defect into a Fourier-multiplier quadratic form, yielding $J$-uniform bounds both for affine warps, with a logarithmic loss in the Haar case, and for $C^2$ warps with $C^{1,\delta}$ generators, and hence a scale-uniform Mallat-type stability estimate for $\Phi$. With the standard child pair, the Hilbert component of the averaged shift nearly cancels for smooth Daubechies-type generators; re-indexing the children by integers restores this component. For Haar and general warps, numerical computations agree with a conjectured $J$-uniform bound.
item.dc:creator: Daewon Chung

item.title: Necessary conditions for the boundedness of directional maximal operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.33980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a set of directions $\Omega$, we investigate whether the associated directional maximal operator $M\_\Omega$ is bounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$, for $p>1$. One can associate to $\Omega$ a numerical quantity called its \textit{Perron capacity}. If the latter is finite, then $M\_\Omega$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for $p \geq 1$. In this paper, we generalize a method introduced by D'Aniello, Gauvan and Moonens to compute the Perron capacity of oscillatory sets of directions such as \[ \Omega\_{\mathrm{cos}} = \left \{\frac{\cos (n)}{n}\,: n \in \NN^*\right \}. \] In a second part, using geometric arguments, we show that if the Minkowski dimension of $\Omega$ is positive, then $M\_\Omega$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for a small range of $p>1$.
item.dc:creator: Bastien Lecluse

item.title: A Perturbative Two-Eigenvalue Faber-Krahn Problem for the Gaussian Short-Time Fourier Transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.33401v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every fixed s\in (0,\infty), the set of area s maximizing the weighted sum of the first two eigenvalues of the associated Toeplitz operators on the Fock space must be a disc, up to translations and sets of measure zero. To do so, we first prove the existence of maximizer sets. Then we show that every maximizer set must be a perturbation of a disc when the weight is sufficiently small. Finally, we use the vector-valued version of the analytic implicit function theorem and the inverse function theorem to conclude that the perturbation must vanish when the weight tends to zero.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Zhang

item.title: Martingale averages, Fourier extension and the Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.33608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The martingale averaged Fourier extension theorem holds for the paraboloid in n dimensions on the Knapp line. Using embedding and interpolation, this gives the complete range of possible exponents (the diagonal case p=q was obtained in [Saw7] using smooth Alpert wavelets instead). OpenAI has recently announced proofs of the deterministic analogue on the diagonal p=q [Ope] and of the local smoothing conjecture [OpeLS], in all dimensions. Since a deterministic estimate at a point on the Knapp line implies the probabilistic one there, the point of the present paper is a short, elementary and self-contained proof of the probabilistic estimate, which uses no Kakeya-type input. We give an application of the probabilistic Knapp theorem to the global initial value problem for the Schr\"odinger equation, in which we obtain sharp regularity results averaged over martingale transforms of the initial data f.
item.dc:creator: Lyudmila Korobenko, Cristian Rios, Eric T. Sawyer

item.title: Locatedness, Convexity, and Lebesgue Measurability - a New Development
item.description: arXiv:2607.15558v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Set within Bishop's framework for constructive analysis, this paper contains a radically improved and expanded development of material, first published in 1988, dealing with the link between locatedness and Lebesgue measurability for convex subsets of R^{N}.
item.dc:creator: Douglas S Bridges

item.title: Restriction estimates using multilinear Kakeya
item.description: arXiv:2610.17752v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use multilinear Kakeya estimates to establish restriction estimates for the paraboloid in dimensions $n\ge5$. The proof inserts Zahl's multilinear Kakeya estimate for direction-separated tubes into the two-ends method of Wang and Wu by means of a broad--narrow argument. In several dimensions, including $n=9$, the resulting exponents were the best known before the recent proof of the local smoothing conjecture by OpenAI.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.15970v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$, answering the question of \cite{CLMP}. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Deodhar
